chunks: One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, who said:

We were in Medina, and Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. So I said, 'Shaving it is better,' and Zurara said, 'Plucking it is better.' So we sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he permitted us while he was in the bathhouse waxing, and he had waxed his armpits. So I said to Zurara, 'Does it suffice you?' He said, 'No, perhaps this deed is for him, and it may not be allowed for me that I should do it.'

So he (peace be upon him) said, 'In what (discussion) are you two?' So I said, 'Zurara is disputing with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. I said shaving is better, and Zurara said plucking is better.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'You have hit the Sunnah and Zurara has erred. Shaving it is better than plucking it, and waxing it is better than shaving it.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said to us, 'Get the waxing done.' So we said, 'We did that three days ago.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Repeat it, for the waxing is cleanliness.'
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for removing armpit hair according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the dispute between Zuraarah and the narrator regarding armpit hair removal by establishing a clear hierarchy: waxing (tila') is superior to shaving, which in turn is superior to plucking. The Imam further instructs them to repeat the waxing, emphasizing that the act of applying wax is itself a form of ritual purity (taharah), thereby linking physical grooming directly to spiritual cleanliness. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imam’s personal practices often reveal deeper jurisprudential wisdom and preferred methods (afdaliyyah) for the community.

en.sarwar: 6. Certain persons of our people have narrated from ibn Jumhur from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn from ‘Abd Allah ibn abu Ya’fur who has said the following:

“Once we were in al-Madinah. Zurarah insisted about plucking out or shaving the hairs of underarms. I said shaving is better and he said, plucking out is better. We asked permission to see abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Permission was granted and he was in the shower applying the paste (to remove hairs). He (the Imam) had applied it to his underarms. I said to Zurarah that it is sufficient. He said, ‘Perhaps he (the Imam) did what was not permissible for me to do.’

He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is the issue between you two people?’ I replied, ‘Zurarah insists about plucking out or shaving.’ I said to him that shaving is better and Zurarah says that plucking out is better. He (the Imam) said, ‘You have found the Sunnah and Zurarah has missed it. Shaving is better than plucking it out, and using paste is better than shaving.’
He (the Imam) then said apply paste. We said, ‘It is three days that we have applied it. He (the Imam) said, ‘Apply again; applying paste is cleansing.’”
